source_note: Entries below come from an Instrumentl opportunity-match export supplied by the org on 2026-08-19, which supersedes the earlier web-search results. Deadlines and amounts are as listed in that export. Where a deadline had no year, it was read as 2026 (today is 2026-08-19). Eligibility fit is this system's assessment, not the funder's — confirm against each NOFO before investing writing time.
correction: The 2026-08-19 web-search run recorded HFNJ Standard Grants as closing 2026-08-28. The export shows 2026-11-19. The Aug 28 date was an unverified search snippet and is wrong.

tier_1_act_now.title: BJA FY2026 Second Chance Act: Improving Reentry Education and Employment Outcomes
tier_1_act_now.funder: US DOJ, Bureau of Justice Assistance
tier_1_act_now.summary: Directly on mission: reentry services for justice-involved people, with education and employment outcomes. Nonprofit community-based organizations are eligible. The org's NJ recovery court, IDRC, and reentry partnerships are exactly the local infrastructure these solicitations expect applicants to have.
tier_1_act_now.watch_out: Award size (up to $1M) is 3x the org's annual budget. Federal reviewers weigh organizational capacity heavily; a sub-award or partnership role with a larger lead applicant may score better than a solo bid.

tier_1_act_now.title: BJA FY2026 Second Chance Act: Family-Based Substance Use Disorder Treatment Program
tier_1_act_now.funder: US DOJ, Bureau of Justice Assistance
tier_1_act_now.summary: Intersects three of the org's focus areas at once — SUD, family/community resilience, and justice involvement. Same deadline as the reentry education solicitation.
tier_1_act_now.watch_out: Titled a 'Treatment Program'. The org delivers psychoeducation and wraparound support and connects clients to outpatient/IOP treatment rather than providing treatment directly. Confirm whether the NOFO requires the applicant to deliver clinical treatment itself, or accepts a treatment-partner structure.

tier_1_act_now.title: Empower New Jersey Grant
tier_1_act_now.summary: NJ-statewide, award size proportionate to a $300k-budget org (roughly 17-33% of annual budget), foundation rather than federal so the compliance lift is far lighter than the BJA solicitations. Best effort-to-probability ratio on this list.

tier_1_act_now.title: Champions in Action Grant
tier_1_act_now.summary: Flat $50k award, corporate foundation. Typically themed by cause area each cycle — worth checking whether this round's theme covers behavioral health or reentry.

tier_1_act_now.title: Standard Grants
tier_1_act_now.funder: The Healthcare Foundation of New Jersey
tier_1_act_now.summary: Greater Newark plus the Greater MetroWest footprint (Essex, Morris, Somerset, Union, parts of Sussex) — overlaps three of four priority counties. Reported recent emphasis on youth and behavioral health.
tier_1_act_now.watch_out: Confirm whether an org with no Jewish Federation affiliation qualifies under the 'targeted vulnerable populations elsewhere in Essex, Morris, and Union' clause.

tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.title: Pathways to Recovery
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.funder: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.summary: Services for NJ residents impacted by opioid use; nonprofits connected to MH/OUD treatment centers eligible, which the org's provider partnerships support. Round 2 NGO track has an LOI deadline of 2027-03-26.

tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.title: Pathways to Recovery - Round 2 NGO
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.funder: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.summary: NGO-specific track of the above — likely the more appropriate door for this org than the general round.

tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.title: General Operating and Project Grants
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.summary: Essex County-focused health funder. General operating support is rare and disproportionately valuable for a small org — unrestricted money funds the infrastructure project grants won't.

tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.title: Specific Population Community Grant Competitive
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.summary: State health funding explicitly aimed at community organizations serving specific populations — the justice-involved population qualifies as one.

tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.funder: NJ Department of Labor and Workforce Development
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.summary: Employment pathways; reentry employment is a natural framing given the org's justice-involved population.

tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.funder: NJ Department of Law & Public Safety

tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.title: Empowerment Grant
tier_2_strong_fit_later_deadline.summary: NJ bank foundation, modest award, low application burden relative to federal work.

watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.title: Adult Reentry Program
watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.amount: Up to $400,000 total costs per year
watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.summary: Purpose is close to a verbatim description of this org's mission: expand SUD treatment and related recovery and reentry services to sentenced adults with SUD and/or co-occurring disorders returning to family and community after incarceration. Private nonprofits are explicitly eligible, and the $400k/yr ceiling is far better matched to a $300k budget than the $1M Second Chance Act tracks.
watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.verify_before_acting: Last confirmed announcement is TI-23-006 (pre-2025). No FY2026 cycle surfaced in search. Check the SAMHSA grants dashboard for an FY2026/FY2027 reissue.

watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.title: Improving Adult and Youth Crisis Stabilization and Community Reentry Program
watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.funder: US DOJ, Bureau of Justice Assistance
watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.summary: Funds clinical services and evidence-based activities to improve reentry and address treatment/recovery needs for people with mental health, substance use, or co-occurring disorders who are or were justice-involved. Nonprofits are eligible WITH OR WITHOUT 501(c)(3) status.
watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.why_it_matters: Eligibility requires nonprofits to apply IN PARTNERSHIP with the relevant criminal or juvenile justice agency. That is not a barrier here - it is the org's existing advantage, given the NJ recovery court and IDRC relationships, and it independently supports the partner-led strategy already recommended for the Second Chance Act tracks.
watch_list_no_confirmed_cycle.verify_before_acting: Only FY23 and FY25 cycles surfaced. Check bja.ojp.gov for a current solicitation.

open_verification_flags.item: BJA Second Chance Act tracks (tier_1, deadline 2026-09-24)
open_verification_flags.flag: Two independent searches on 2026-08-20 failed to corroborate a 2026-09-24 deadline. Search surfaced only the FY25 cycle (closed 2026-05-11) and FY24. The 2026-09-24 date comes solely from the Instrumentl export supplied 2026-08-19.
open_verification_flags.assessment: Not a contradiction - Instrumentl tracks live opportunities and archived agency pages dominate search results. But the date has no second source, and SAM.gov registration timing is being planned around it.
open_verification_flags.action: Confirm directly at bja.ojp.gov or grants.gov before committing writing time or treating 2026-09-24 as the SAM.gov registration deadline.

open_verification_flags.flag: Search indicates nonprofit applicants for federal reentry funding are typically expected to demonstrate 2-3 years of operational experience in justice-related or workforce programming, and some programs require formal partnership with correctional, probation, or parole agencies.
open_verification_flags.action: Confirm the org meets the operational-history bar before investing in a solo federal application. The partnership requirement is already satisfied in substance by the court/IDRC relationships.
